From the graph, the two curves are standard sinusoids of equal amplitude and period \(2\pi\), specifically of the forms
\[
y_1=\frac52\cos x,\qquad y_2=\frac52\sin x
\]
(up to swapping the labels).

For an intersection,
\[
\frac52\cos x=\frac52\sin x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\cos x=\sin x
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\tan x=1.
\]
Thus
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{4}+k\pi.
\]
Within the interval \([0,2\pi]\), this gives
\[
x=\frac{\pi}{4}\quad\text{and}\quad x=\frac{5\pi}{4}.
\]
These correspond to two distinct intersection points. The red points on the \(x\)-axis are \(x\)-intercepts of the individual curves, not common intersection points of the two curves.

\[
\boxed{\text{The two curves have }2\text{ intersection points in }[0,2\pi].}
\]

(Equivalently, the intersection points are \(\left(\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\sqrt2}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},-\frac{5\sqrt2}{4}\right)\).)
